hubDescription: Tree service in Lebanon, TN and Wilson County: tree removal, trimming, stump grinding, storm cleanup and land clearing. Licensed, insured, free estimates. Call 615-561-0472.
hubIntro: Lebanon was named for the red cedar that once covered the area, and locals still call it Cedar City. Founded in 1802 as the Wilson County seat, it centers on the Lebanon Public Square and Cumberland University, with older residential streets lined with established shade trees and newer growth spreading out along the I-40 corridor, Highway 231 and Hartmann Drive.

Triple Oak Services is based in Nashville and travels to Lebanon for tree removal, tree trimming and pruning, stump grinding, storm damage cleanup and land clearing. This page covers what tree work in Lebanon tends to involve, why red cedar and limestone soil matter, and what to know before you hire a crew. Every job starts with a free, no-obligation estimate.

sections.h2: Cedar City: red cedar and limestone soil
paragraphs: Eastern red cedar defines Lebanon's landscape. The cedar glades around Cedars of Lebanon State Park, about ten miles south of town, are a nationally recognized natural landmark, and the cedars that gave the city its nickname still grow on rocky ground, fence lines and abandoned lots across Wilson County. Red cedar is tough, but it is also a fast, aggressive volunteer that can take over a lot left alone for a few seasons.

The ground in this part of the county is limestone, often with only a thin layer of soil over rock. That matters for trees. Shallow soil keeps roots from going deep, so many healthy trees have wide, shallow root plates that can lift in saturated ground or high wind. Cedars that grow tall and dense along a property line, or hardwoods on a thin-soiled slope, are the ones that tend to lean and fall without any obvious rot in the trunk.

sections.h2: Around the Square, Cumberland University and the older streets
paragraphs: Lebanon's historic core is built around the Public Square, with Cumberland University a short distance away and older neighborhoods along West Main Street and Castle Heights. Mature oaks, maples and hickories grow beside houses that are a century old or more, and their crowns now reach over roofs, porches and overhead service lines. Tight lots, old fences and limited access make removals here close-quarters work, with trees coming down in sections and cleanup done with care.

Because older trees are part of what makes these streets attractive, we are glad to talk through crown cleaning, thinning and hazard reduction before recommending removal. When a tree is dead, diseased or leaning toward a building, we explain the safest way to take it down and what the job includes.

sections.h2: Growth along I-40, Highway 231 and Hartmann Drive
paragraphs: Lebanon has grown well past its old town limits, with new subdivisions, shopping centers and distribution sites along I-40, Highway 231 and Hartmann Drive. Many sit on former farmland and woodland. Builders often leave a few big trees standing, but their roots can be cut or buried during construction, and they can decline years later. New landscaping trees planted too close to houses can crowd foundations as they grow.

Larger lots toward the edges of the city and out on roads like Sparta Pike and Jefferson Pike bring bigger jobs: tree lines that have never been thinned, cedar thickets on back property, and brush that needs clearing before a barn, a pool or a driveway goes in. Those jobs often combine removal, stump grinding and land clearing in one visit.

sections.h2: Before you remove a tree in Lebanon
paragraphs: Rules can depend on whether your property is inside the city or in unincorporated Wilson County, on any development approvals attached to it, and on HOA covenants. Street trees and trees in the public right-of-way cannot be removed by a homeowner or contractor. Check with the City of Lebanon and your HOA before removing a large tree, and confirm current requirements rather than relying on what a neighbor did.

Look up before work begins. Trees touching or close to power lines should be handled by the utility or a qualified line-clearance crew, and anyone in danger should call 911. If stump grinding or digging is involved, call Tennessee 811 so buried utilities are marked. We point out lines, fences, septic fields and structures when we quote.

We are a locally owned, licensed and insured company. For Lebanon jobs we give a free estimate, explain how the tree will come down and what the price includes, remove it safely and haul the debris away. Stump grinding can be added on the same visit, and storm damage and emergency removal are available when a tree is already down. If trimming will do the job, we will tell you.

hubFaq.q: Do you provide tree service in Lebanon, TN?
hubFaq.a: Yes. Triple Oak Services travels from Nashville to Lebanon and the surrounding Wilson County area for tree removal, trimming and pruning, stump grinding, storm damage cleanup and land clearing in the 37087 and 37090 zip codes.

hubFaq.q: Can you remove red cedar trees and thickets?
hubFaq.a: Yes. Red cedar is common across Lebanon and grows quickly on fence lines and untended lots. We remove individual trees and clear thickets, and we can grind stumps and haul the debris.

hubFaq.q: Why do healthy trees blow over in Lebanon?
hubFaq.a: Limestone is close to the surface in much of Wilson County, so many trees have shallow, wide root systems. Saturated ground and strong winds can lift those roots, and a tree can fall without any visible rot.

hubFaq.q: Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Lebanon?
hubFaq.a: It depends on whether you are inside city limits, any development approvals and HOA rules. Street and right-of-way trees cannot be removed by homeowners. Check with the City of Lebanon before removing a large tree.

tree-trimming-pruning.title: Tree Trimming & Pruning in Lebanon, TN | Triple Oak Services
tree-trimming-pruning.description: Tree trimming and pruning in Lebanon, TN: dead limb removal, crown thinning, clearance from roofs and lines, storm-risk reduction. Licensed, insured. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: Shade trees are a big part of Lebanon's older streets, and they stay healthy and safe with regular pruning. Removing dead wood, thinning heavy crowns and shortening overextended limbs lowers the chance of a branch failing over a roof or car, particularly on trees with shallow root systems that take wind harder.

Common trimming calls include limbs over roofs and gutters, branches pushing against siding, and trees crowding service lines. In newer communities along Hartmann Drive and Highway 231, young trees often need structural pruning early so they grow with one strong leader instead of splitting in a storm.
We do not top trees. We explain what will be removed and why before any cutting begins.

faq.q: Can you thin a cedar that has grown too dense?
faq.a: Yes. Overgrown cedars can be thinned and limbed up, though some are better removed. We will tell you which makes sense.

faq.q: How often should my trees be trimmed?
faq.a: Many mature trees benefit from a check every few years. Dead wood and limbs over structures should be handled as soon as you notice them.

stump-grinding.title: Stump Grinding in Lebanon, TN | Triple Oak Services
stump-grinding.description: Stump grinding in Lebanon, TN: stumps ground below grade, root flare removal and cleanup so your yard is ready to use. Free estimates. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: A stump left after a removal is hard to mow around and holds moisture that attracts insects and fungus. We grind stumps below grade in Lebanon so the spot can be filled and planted, from a small stump in an in-town yard to a large cedar or oak stump on acreage toward Sparta Pike or Jefferson Pike.

Limestone close to the surface can make grinding slower, since rocky ground is harder on equipment and wide, shallow root flares often have to be ground out along with the stump. We look at the stump, the roots and the access during the estimate and size the job to match.
Call Tennessee 811 before digging or grinding so buried utilities are marked. Stump grinding pairs well with removal, so ask about doing both on the same visit.

faq.q: Does rocky ground make stump grinding harder?
faq.a: It can. Shallow limestone affects how roots grow and how the machine works, which is why we assess each stump before pricing.
Yes. Cedar stumps are common in Lebanon, and we grind them below grade like any other.

storm-damage-cleanup.title: Storm Damage Tree Cleanup in Lebanon, TN | Emergency Removal | Triple Oak Services
storm-damage-cleanup.description: Storm damage tree cleanup in Lebanon, TN: fallen trees, hanging limbs and emergency removal, including same-day service when available. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: Thunderstorms and straight-line winds are the usual cause of storm damage in Lebanon. Because soil is thin over limestone, whole trees can lift out at the roots instead of snapping, and tall cedars and hardwoods on exposed ground are among the first to come down across driveways, fences and roofs.

If a tree is down, make everyone safe first. If a power line is involved or anyone is in danger, call 911 and your utility, then call us. We provide storm damage and emergency tree removal, including same-day emergency removal where scheduling allows, and we clear trees and limbs from roofs, yards and driveways.
After a storm, check the trees that stayed standing for cracks, loosened soil and hanging branches, and have them checked before the next one.

faq.q: Do you do emergency tree removal in Lebanon?
faq.a: Yes, including same-day emergency removal after storms when scheduling allows. Call 615-561-0472.

faq.q: Why do whole trees fall instead of breaking?
faq.a: Shallow soil over limestone limits root depth, so roots can lift when the ground is saturated and winds are strong.

paragraphs: Land clearing in Lebanon often starts with cedar. Eastern red cedar spreads fast on untended ground, and a back lot, fence line or pasture edge can turn into a dense thicket in just a few seasons. We clear cedar, brush and undergrowth, remove trees in the way and grind stumps if needed.

Other common jobs include clearing building sites along Highway 231, Hartmann Drive and the I-40 corridor, opening up driveways on larger lots toward Sparta Pike and Jefferson Pike, and cleaning up property lines. We walk the property first and give you a clear price before work begins.
If clearing is part of a build, check with the City of Lebanon or Wilson County about permits and approvals. We clear to the lines you mark.

faq.q: Can you clear a cedar thicket?
faq.a: Yes. Cedar thickets are one of the most common land clearing jobs in Lebanon, and we remove them along with brush and stumps as needed.

faq.q: Do you clear lots for construction?
faq.a: Yes. We clear brush, trees and stumps so a lot is ready for the next step. Permits for the build itself are separate.
